title: The photo album
grammar: past simple + when I was little

scene.speaker: valentina
scene.bubble: Grandma's photo album! Look — my mum when she was little… with the SAME smile as me!
scene.intro: Grandma's photo album is open on the table. Look — this is Valentina's mother when she was little, with a huge hat. Here is grandpa with his first bicycle. In this photo Erik was a baby and he was already looking at a machine. They laugh, they remember, and they take a new photo for the album. What were YOU like when you were little?

activities.title: Match the photo with the moment.

pairs.left: a baby with a tiny hat
a boy with a toy robot
a puppy in a shoe box

activities.title: Quick check · Choose was or were.

items.sentence: When I ___ little, I had curly hair.
My grandparents ___ very young in this photo.
___ you a quiet baby? — No! I cried a lot.
The photos ___ black and white in grandpa's time.

activities.title: Listen to the album afternoon. Write a word or number in each gap.

data.voice_note: Voces: Valentina (con el álbum) y Erik (invitado curioso).
data.script: Valentina: This album is forty years old. Grandma keeps it in a wooden box. … Erik: Look! Is that your mum on a horse? … Valentina: Yes! She was seven. It was her uncle's farm. … Erik: And this baby with the enormous cake? … Valentina: Me! My first birthday. I put my whole hand in the cake. … Erik: Classic! Who took all these photos? … Valentina: Grandpa, with his old silver camera. He still has it! … Valentina: Grandma says: photos keep the smiles safe forever.

data.text: Describe a family photo you love (from memory): who was there, where it was, why you like it. Your partner asks 2 questions.

activities.title: A and B are not the same. Find out why!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 12 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Ask your family for an old photo. Write 4 sentences: who, where, when, and one funny detail. Use was/were.

outcomes.puede: Understand longer dialogues (Movers parts 1–5); identify specific info in spoken texts.
Describe places, objects, past events; role-play simple situations.
Read and sequence short stories; locate information in signs, notices.
Write a note/message of 30–40 words (Movers Writing part); classroom paragraphs 60–100w.
